messages.subject: Question on psi average
parts:
Dear list members,

I sent the following questions to Richard thinking that were not appropriate for the list but Richard suggested me to post it to the list.

Question;

When doing occupancy models and using covariates I have seen people take an average of the occupancy on all the sites to give an unique value of psi.  Is that correct?  How do you get a EE for that approach?  Is it an alternative to take the average of the covariate and plug-in that value in the formula of the best model?


Richard answer:

Hi Manuel, 

This would be a good question for the list as I'm sure other people have the same question. Anyhow, the approach you mention is fine, but if you only want to make know what proportion of the sites *in the sample* were occupied, it would be better to use the new ranef() function. Something like: 

re <- ranef(fm) 
mean(bup(re, stat="mode")) 
colMeans(confint(re)) 

Richard 



Best,

Manuel
